title: Absolute Galois presentation of the fundamental group of a normal integral scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a normal integral scheme: it is integral in the sense of [def-pc-integral-scheme] and every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Write $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ for its function field at its generic point $\eta$, and choose a separable closure $\Omega/K$ [def-pd-separable-closure]. Put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ with its profinite Krull topology. Choose an algebraic closure $\widetilde\Omega$ containing $\Omega$; automorphisms of $\Omega$ extend uniquely over the purely inseparable extension $\widetilde\Omega/\Omega$. For each $x\in X$, choose a strict henselization $A_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and a compatible $K$-embedding of its fraction field $K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}$ into $\Omega$. These strict henselizations are domains and such embeddings exist. Set $J_x=\operatorname{Aut}_{K_x^{\mathrm{sh}}}(\Omega)\subseteq G$. Then the homomorphism $q_X:G\to\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)$ induced by $\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, with geometric generic point $\bar\eta=\operatorname{Spec}\widetilde\Omega$ and fundamental group as in [def-galois-fibre-functor], is continuous and surjective, and $\ker(q_X)$ is the smallest closed normal subgroup of $G$ containing all $J_x$. This holds for any such choices of the embeddings.

proof.text: Apply the fully faithful field-point lemma to $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$: $X$ is connected since it is integral, and generic-point full faithfulness supplies its hypothesis for all finite etale covers. It constructs the unique extensions to $\widetilde\Omega$ and the canonical continuous surjection $q_X:G\to\Pi=\pi_1(X,\bar\eta)$, with the required action on every geometric fibre.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia, finite-quotient proof; Tag 0BQM, proposition-normal.

proof.text: The strict-local comparison supplies the domains and compatible embeddings. Put $N$ equal to the closed normal closure of the chosen $J_x$. Each $J_x$ acts trivially on every finite etale geometric generic fibre. Since elements of $\Pi$ are natural automorphisms of the fibre functor, this says $q_X(J_x)=1$. The kernel is closed and normal, so $N\subseteq\ker q_X$. The same comparison says that every normalization inertia subgroup on any affine open is conjugate to the corresponding $J_x$, hence is contained in $N$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia, finite-quotient proof; setup and proof.

proof.text: Let $U$ be any open normal subgroup of $G$ containing $N$. On each nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the strict-local comparison makes $A$ an integrally closed domain with fraction field $K$ and puts every infinite-level inertia inside $U$. Apply the fixed-field inertia lemma: $L=\Omega^U$ is finite Galois, $U=\operatorname{Aut}_L(\Omega)$, and all primes of the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ have trivial inertia. This holds on every $V$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia, finite-quotient proof; setup and proof.

proof.text: Apply the trivial-inertia normalization lemma to $L/K$. It gives a finite etale cover $Y\to X$ whose geometric generic fibre has a point with $G$-stabilizer $\operatorname{Aut}_L(\Omega)=U$. Every element of $\ker q_X$ acts identically on this fibre, so fixes that point; thus $\ker q_X\subseteq U$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia, finite-quotient proof; setup and proof.

proof.text: Profinite subgroup separation expresses $N$ as the intersection of its open overgroups $W$. Each has finitely many cosets. The coset action has open normal kernel $U_W\subseteq W$; normality of $N$ gives $g^{-1}ng\in N\subseteq W$ for every $n\in N$, so $N\subseteq U_W$. Hence the intersection of the open normal overgroups is also $N$. Step 4 places $\ker q_X$ in this intersection and step 2 gives equality. Changing embeddings conjugates each $J_x$ by the strict-local comparison, preserving their closed normal closure. The result holds for every choice.
